title: If/else
explain: An if/else statement lets your program make decisions based on conditions. If a condition is true, the code in the if block runs; otherwise, the code in the else block runs. You can check conditions using comparison operators like ==, >, <, and !=.
exercise: Write a program that asks the user for their favorite color, then prints a different message based on whether it's 'blue' or not.
tip: Remember to use == (double equals) to compare values, not = (single equals) which assigns values. For example, use if x == 5: not if x = 5:
